key_insight: Burst restarts in wall turbulence can be explained by a forced linearized model where nonlinear effects mainly supply enough available energy and vortex rearrangement for the next burst to begin.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more structure-agnostic way to model and predict burst regeneration in wall-bounded flows, which is useful for turbulence control and reduced-order modeling.
method: Formulated a forced linearized Navier–Stokes system for a log-minimal channel.
Solved optimization problems to find minimal conditions for burst-restart-like solutions.
Introduced linearly available energy (LAE) to track the restart process via vortex breakup and catch-up stages.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analysis of both forced linear models and flow patterns extracted from real turbulence during restarting stages, showing consistent breakup and merging effects.
watch_item: The LAE framework is model-dependent and derived from a reduced log-minimal channel setup, so its transferability to broader turbulent flows may need validation.
paper_title: Restarts of bursts in turbulence in a log-minimal channel
